City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Attorney Steve McEwen
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Development/Public Works Director Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

None.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  HUFF, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-E AS FOLLOWS BY THE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 14, 2025
 8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  INTRODUCTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 755 ESTABLISHING A PERMIT
  PROCEDURE AND REGULATIONS FOR COMMERCIAL AND STUDENT FILMING

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Introduce for a first reading, Ordinance
  No. 755; and 2) Direct staff to bring back Ordinance No. 755 for a second reading
  and adoption at the City Council meeting of October 28, 2025.

Community Development & Public Works Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per
the agenda material).

Director Naughton explained that the ordinance is based on the model film ordinance
created by the California Film Commission, creating consistency across the region and state,
in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

Director Naughton confirmed the fees will not increase and some would decrease with the
proposed ordinance, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also confirmed that fees are reduced for student filming.

Naughton explained that at the City Council’s next meeting, staff plans to bring back a
Resolution to amend the permit fee schedule including the regular permit fee, reduced
student film fee and expedited review fee, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
SCHACHTER.

Director Naughton explained that staff is currently exploring per-day fees, as opposed to the
current flat fee for filming, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN. MAYOR PRO
TEM ZERUNYAN emphasized the impacts of multi-day productions as compared to a single
day shoot, including noise, pollution, multiple trailers etc.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  1) INTRODUCE FOR A FIRST READING, ORDINANCE NO. 755; AND 2)
  DIRECT STAFF TO BRING BACK ORDINANCE NO. 755 FOR A SECOND
  READING AND ADOPTION AT THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING OF OCTOBER
  28, 2025.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 755 by title.

B.  RESOLUTION NO. 2610 ADOPTION OF STAND-ALONE PROCUREMENT
  POLICIES PERTAINING TO FEDERALLY FUNDED PROCUREMENTS, CREDIT
  CARD USAGE, AND THE PROCUREMENT OF ORGANIC WASTE AND RECYCLED
  PRODUCTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2610 approving three
  stand-alone policies to be incorporated as exhibits to the City’s Procurement Policy.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 14, 2025
   COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2610 APPROVING THREE STAND-ALONE
  POLICIES TO BE INCORPORATED AS EXHIBITS TO THE CITY’S
  PROCUREMENT POLICY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2610 by title.

C.  COMMISSION AND COMMITTEE LOCAL APPOINTMENT  LIST  AND
  APPOINTMENT PROCESS FOR EXPIRING TERMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the Commission/Committee
  appointment process for expiring terms, and receive and file this report.

City Clerk Pettit provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF requested that a column be added to the Local Appointment List
showing the original appointment dates of each Commissioner and Committee Member.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER requested that the Commission and Committee
attendance report be available to the City Council before reappointments are made.

Discussion ensued about whether or not to interview all Commissioners and Committee
Members or just new applicants. It was the consensus of the City Council to only interview new
applicants this year.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

MAYOR STEGURA so ordered.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the Cal Cities Annual Conference last week along with
MAYOR STEGURA, COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER and City staff and interviewed
Lieutenant Governor Eleni Kounalakis at the Los Angeles County Division Annual Conference
Lunch.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also participated in the Cal Cities webinar regarding grants
available for parks, along with City staff, as well as the PV Village “Upside of Aging” event.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also attended the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of
Commerce’s Annual Legislative Forum and Luncheon on September 26 with City Manager
Greg Grammer at the Palos Verdes Golf Club.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER noted that Assistant City Manager Davis spoke on a panel
at the Cal Cities Conference last week, and that she plans to attend the Palos Verdes Peninsula
Transit Board meeting tomorrow night.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 14, 2025
 MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN reported that Assistant City Manager Davis and Assistant to
the City Manager Slawson both presented at the USC Price School’s Mayors and Council
Members Local Leaders Forum on October 4.

MAYOR STEGURA attended the South Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG) Board
meeting on September 25, as well as the Clean Power Alliance retreat on September 26 along
with Community Development and Public Works Director Naughton.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

MAYOR STEGURA thanked Tracy Austin, sponsors, attendees, City staff for their participation
at the 46th annual Tracy Austin Doubles Tennis Tournament.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:26 p.m. MAYOR STEGURA adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, October 28, 2025 at
7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Debby Stegura, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 14, 2025
